contrast_detail: video-induced session: positive valence (joy/tenderness/inspiration) vs negative valence (sadness/disgust/fear); neutral dropped; 9 positive + 9 negative 30 s trials per subject
note: affective-valence generalization cohort, erasure diagnostic only; NOT part of the 2x2 panel; 4th consensus-marker family (emotional valence)
headline_finding: SUB-GATE / BOUNDARY COHORT (not a failed replication). Cross-subject valence decoding from frozen FM features over 4 s windows is at chance (raw label BA 0.51-0.53) for ALL 3 FMs -- below the a-priori 0.55 interpretability gate -- so Delta_erase is UNINTERPRETABLE here. The LEACE machinery functions correctly: subject identity is strongly encoded (linear subj-BA 0.62/0.70/0.98 for cbramod/labram/reve) and cleanly erased to chance (->0.001/0.001/0.003). The consensus marker simply isn't decodable in this regime, so the gate correctly returns 'inconclusive' rather than a positive result. Erasure-helps is therefore NEITHER confirmed NOR refuted on the affective family -- it is UNTESTABLE with frozen FM features under cross-subject CV. This is a scope/falsifiability finding: erasure-helps replicates on the 3 families where the marker clears the gate (arithmetic theta, motor ERD, auditory P300); on the affective family the marker fails the gate, so the test cannot run. The gate does its job. Per the locked a-priori protocol we do NOT relax the gate, switch to within-subject CV, lengthen windows, or change the montage to manufacture a positive result.
preprocess: VENDOR-PREPROCESSED (NOT preprocess_v2): bandpass 0.5-47 Hz, 200 Hz, FastICA n=60 (manual exclusion), 64-ch average reference; COMMON_19 selected by name; 4 s windows over the 30 s trials
caveats: METHODOLOGY DEVIATION (the only cohort that does NOT use preprocess_v2): ds005540 ships no raw EEG, only vendor-preprocessed arrays. The vendor pipeline is bandpass 0.5-47 Hz -> 200 Hz -> FastICA n=60 (manual component exclusion) -> 64-ch average reference. preprocess_v2's ICLabel + autoreject + CAR + COMMON_19-during-ICA were NOT applied; we select COMMON_19 by name post-hoc. Cross-cohort cleaning is therefore NOT identical here (user-authorised choice).
emotional valence is a SUSTAINED, endogenous affective state, not a stimulus-locked ERP/ERD; it is the most diffuse and (a-priori) hardest-to-decode of the four families.
labels are CATEGORY-derived (joy/tenderness/inspiration = positive; sadness/disgust/fear = negative); neutral dropped. We do NOT use the continuous 10-item ratings.
30 s trials windowed into 4 s segments; 9 positive + 9 negative trials per subject (balanced by design).
sub01-54 (complete 21-trial sessions) only; sub55-60 excluded (missing trials).
subj-BA chance floor 1/n_subj differs across cohorts; use subj-BA/chance ratio.

REVE: near-perfect subject ID (0.976) erased to chance (0.003); post-erasure label BA 0.673 WOULD clear the gate, but the a-priori protocol requires RAW BA >= 0.55, which REVE fails at 0.528. The gate enforces no rescue; we do not cite the +14.5 pp.

NARROW CLAIM: the null is 'cross-SUBJECT frozen-FM valence decoding ~ chance on ds005540', NOT 'valence is absent from this EEG'. The dataset paper reports 66.7% binary pos/neg but CROSS-CONTEXT (train one context, test the other) with handcrafted DE/PSD features + SVM; cross-context != our cross-subject split, so it does not contradict this null.
COMMON_19 montage drops AF3/AF4 (frontal-asymmetry valence markers); F3/F4 are kept. Possible information loss, but the montage is locked across all cohorts -- not tuned here.
